nodes.label: Comparativa Chatbot vs LumatAgent
nodes.rationale: Chatbot y LumatAgent resuelven problemas distintos (atención HOY vs gestión/crecimiento MAÑANA); la elección depende de necesidades actuales y futuras.

nodes.label: Opción A — Chatbot IA
nodes.rationale: Opción más rápida y económica ($1,000-1,500); solo atención por WhatsApp; agregar automatizaciones en el futuro exigiría reestructurar la arquitectura (costo adicional).

nodes.label: Derivación a atención humana
nodes.rationale: La derivación incluye el historial completo — el cliente no repite información.

nodes.label: Opción A — Chatbot IA (monolítico)
nodes.rationale: Más rápida y económica ($4,000-4,400), pero requiere rediseño si se quiere expandir a automatizaciones, agenda o agentes internos.

nodes.label: Opción B — Base Multi-Agente + WhatsApp (recomendada)
nodes.rationale: Construye la base multi-agente desde el inicio para escalar sin reescribir; cuando Lumat quiera activar Calendar/Automation/Notification/Report Agents no se reescribe nada.

nodes.label: Recomendación: Opción B del Milestone 1
nodes.rationale: Opción B ($1,500–2,000 USD, 6–8 semanas) es la mejor relación costo-beneficio: WhatsApp funcional desde el día 1, arquitectura multi-agente lista para crecer sin reescribir código; cuesta solo $500 más que la Opción A pero evita pagar dos veces por la misma arquitectura.

nodes.label: Anexo A — Flujo Conversacional Completo
nodes.rationale: Especificación funcional del flujo (10 páginas) que cubre cliente nuevo, existente, emergencia, garantía, agendamiento, fuera de horario y escalamiento; da aspecto de propuesta de consultoría.

nodes.label: Anexo B — Glosario Técnico
nodes.rationale: Explica conceptos técnicos (RAG, Embeddings, LangGraph, JWT) porque quien aprueba una propuesta normalmente no es desarrollador.

nodes.label: Anexo C — Cronograma del Proyecto
nodes.rationale: Cronograma ejecutivo por semanas por milestone; da confianza sobre la operación en producción.

nodes.label: Arquitectura Multi-Agente (orquestador LangGraph)
nodes.rationale: Patrón orquestador que coordina agentes especializados (WhatsApp, Calendario, Automatizaciones, Notificaciones, Reportes) con herramientas de permisos granulares; crece de asistente a miembro del equipo sin reescribir.

nodes.label: Activity Event Dots
nodes.rationale: Colored event-type markers: emergency=red, visit=blue, warranty=amber. Instant semantic scanning of feed items without reading text.

nodes.label: Case Status Enum
nodes.rationale: Shared lifecycle states (pendiente/crítico/agendado/finalizado) implied across the cases table, badges, and pending KPI — a common data contract for the admin panel.

nodes.label: Sidebar Navigation
nodes.rationale: Fixed 240px dark-blue sidebar keeps every admin section (Dashboard, Clientes, Conversaciones, Casos, Agenda, Base de Conocimiento, Configuración, Reportes) always reachable; navy anchors the SPA against the light content area.

nodes.label: Header / User Bar
nodes.rationale: Header shows screen title plus current user (Carlos Muñoz — Administrador, avatar CM), reinforcing the admin role context on every screen.

nodes.label: KPI: New Clients
nodes.rationale: Value 18, trend +12% vs previous month. Measures chatbot's customer acquisition effectiveness.

nodes.label: KPI: Emergencies
nodes.rationale: Value 1, flat trend. Surface-level count of gas-leak/emergency events needing urgent dispatch.

nodes.label: KPI Cards Grid
nodes.rationale: Four-card grid (Clientes Nuevos, Solicitudes de Visita, Emergencias, Pendientes) gives at-a-glance operational health; trend arrows compare against previous month (↑ green growth, ↓ red decline, neutral gray).

nodes.label: KPI: Pending Cases
nodes.rationale: Value 6, trend -15% (red). Pending queue is a throughput/backlog signal for ops.

nodes.label: KPI: Visit Requests
nodes.rationale: Value 24, trend +8% vs previous month. Counts service visit requests funneling into scheduling.

nodes.label: Recent Activity Feed
nodes.rationale: Chronological event stream (with timestamps) surfaces urgent events and recent bot-driven requests in real time: emergency reports, visit requests, post-sale warranty, confirmed scheduling.

nodes.label: Recent Cases Table
nodes.rationale: Table format chosen for dense case data (Cliente, Motivo, Estado, Fecha, Técnico). Columns include reason types the chatbot classifies: calefont failure, gas leak, boiler maintenance, warranty, thermostat installation.

nodes.label: Case Status Badges
nodes.rationale: Color-coded badges for fast scanning: crítico=red, pendiente=amber, agendado=blue, finalizado=green. Visual priority encoding replaces raw text.

nodes.label: HH-5 Human Response Channel
nodes.rationale: In H1 the human responds through the same WhatsApp number; replying from the panel is out of scope (H2).

nodes.label: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Ponytail scope: minimal H1 panel served by FastAPI, no PWA, no chart library, no advanced dashboards (H2-H4).

nodes.label: Conversation Manager
nodes.rationale: Single-agent LangGraph flow with persistent per-conversation state; emergency and handoff mechanics live in separate specs.

nodes.label: Emergency Detection
nodes.rationale: Detection runs deterministically before LLM classification; conservative default is escalation, never silent ignore.

nodes.label: Human Handoff
nodes.rationale: H1 scope is deriva + history + summary + case visibility; reply-from-panel is explicitly an H2 deliverable.

nodes.label: Knowledge Base
nodes.rationale: Single authorized source for bot answers; no code changes required to update content; embedding provider/model/cost recorded.

nodes.label: Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Hardens the H1 deployment (Hostinger KVM 2, Ubuntu LTS + Docker Compose) to production-ready state before go-live.

nodes.label: Settings and Scope Limits
nodes.rationale: Lets the owner define bot operational boundaries without code; includes Meta service-message pricing awareness effective 2026-10-01.

nodes.label: Agente WhatsApp Atención al Cliente
nodes.rationale: Front-door agent; sole agent wired to the RAG knowledge base

nodes.label: Sistema de Roles (Dueño | Admin | Técnico | Cliente)
nodes.rationale: RBAC model: tool execution is gated by role, mapping the four user types to capabilities

nodes.label: VPS Hetzner
nodes.rationale: Propiedad total de datos y código, costos predecibles, sin vendor lock-in — requisito explícito del cliente.

nodes.label: admin-panel capability
nodes.rationale: D7: FastAPI + Jinja2 + vanilla JS, signed-cookie sessions, bcrypt — 8 views, server-enforced roles, no client framework; CSV export via stdlib

nodes.label: Cost guardrails (spend limits + alerts)
nodes.rationale: D6: cost columns on messages + SQL SUM instead of separate spend_ledger table — no join, no write path duplication

nodes.label: emergency-detection capability
nodes.rationale: D4: deterministic keyword gate runs before any LLM — safety path avoids latency, cost and false negatives; weak hit conservatively escalates to human (EM-5)

nodes.label: Headless Chrome (Puppeteer) renderer
nodes.rationale: AD3: wireframes pre-rendered to PNG via headless Chrome screenshots — same Puppeteer that md-to-pdf already bundles

nodes.label: knowledge-base capability
nodes.rationale: D8: restore = active_version pointer flip, chunks tagged per version — no re-embedding on restore

nodes.label: LangGraph conversation graph
nodes.rationale: D1/D2: in-process async + startup recovery sweep instead of worker/broker (YAGNI at tens conv/day); no checkpointer — state rebuilt from Postgres per message (messages table is the source of truth)

nodes.label: md-to-pdf engine
nodes.rationale: AD1: chosen over pandoc+weasyprint — already proven on this project (style.css + config.js); headless Chrome renders CSS, tables and images correctly

nodes.label: Mermaid CLI (mmdc)
nodes.rationale: AD2: md-to-pdf cannot render Mermaid, so diagrams are pre-rendered to PNG via mmdc (v11.16.0) and referenced as static images

nodes.label: OpenAI provider (gpt-4o-mini / text-embedding-3-small)
nodes.rationale: D3: single LLM vendor — one key, one cost ledger, one client lib; Spanish quality sufficient at minimum cost

nodes.label: PostgreSQL + pgvector
nodes.rationale: D5: single settings KV table (jsonb) replaces 8 per-domain config tables — config is KV, not relational

nodes.label: propuesta-tecnica-economica-lumat.md
nodes.rationale: AD4: single markdown file chosen over multi-file — 25-30 page linear document, multi-file adds build complexity with no benefit

nodes.label: Customer Records
nodes.rationale: One deduplicated ficha per person, recognized by phone number even across normalized formats.

nodes.label: Audit log (audit_log)
nodes.rationale: Cada acción del agente queda trazada (quién, qué, cuándo); consultable por rol.

nodes.label: Worker de automatizaciones
nodes.rationale: Proceso aparte determinístico (no-LLM) que lee la tabla automations cada N minutos y ejecuta acciones; el agente escribe configuraciones, nunca código.

nodes.label: Tools Layer (whitelist + validación de parámetros)
nodes.rationale: El agente solo hace lo que tiene una tool para hacer: valida permisos, valida parámetros, ejecuta, loguea en audit_log. No existe ejecutar código arbitrario.

nodes.label: Arquitectura agéntica (LLM + Harness + Config + Memoria)
nodes.rationale: Mismo patrón que los coding agents pero adaptado a atención al cliente; un chatbot tradicional con árbol de decisión es rígido, difícil de mantener y no escala.

nodes.label: Memoria Mini-Engram (3 niveles: session/customer/knowledge)
nodes.rationale: 3 niveles: session memory (Redis, working), customer memory (episodic, customer_memo con embedding), knowledge base (semantic, knowledge_chunks vectorizados) + compression pipeline post-conversación.

nodes.label: LumatAgent — coworker digital multi-agente
nodes.rationale: NO es un chatbot: vive en el servidor, entiende procesos de negocio, delega a sub-agentes y crea automatizaciones por lenguaje natural del dueño. La arquitectura multi-agente permite activar sub-agentes sin refactor.

nodes.label: Calendario propio (PostgreSQL, fuente de verdad)
nodes.rationale: La sincronización bidireccional con calendarios externos es un proyecto en sí (conflictos, duplicados, latencia); Apple NO tiene API pública (solo CalDAV frágil). Con fuente de verdad propia las reglas de negocio viven en la DB y el sistema no depende de terceros.

nodes.label: Lumat Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: This wireframe shows the technician schedule screen of the LumatAgent admin panel (WhatsApp chatbot for a Chilean plumbing company). Its purpose is weekly dispatch planning: assigning visits, maintenance and emergencies to technicians per day/time slot.

nodes.label: Blocked Slot (Lunch/Unavailable)
nodes.rationale: Diagonal-hatched cells mark lunch (ALMUERZO, midday in every day) and an unavailable block (Bloqueado on JUE). Blocking slots prevents double-booking during non-work windows.

nodes.label: Weekly Technician Calendar
nodes.rationale: Core layout: a horizontal grid of five day columns (LUN-VIE) aligned against a fixed 70px time column (08:00-18:00). Fixed-height 56px slots keep rows aligned so events read as a time grid.

nodes.label: Schedule Event Block
nodes.rationale: Event blocks carry the customer name and a short job description; a colored left border encodes the type so the schedule is scannable at a glance without reading each block.

nodes.label: Emergency Event Type
nodes.rationale: An 'emergency' color style exists in the design (red) and one event is labeled 'Fuga gas - Emergencia', but that event still uses the blue visit style and the legend omits emergency, so the emergency treatment is ambiguous.

nodes.label: Maintenance Event Type
nodes.rationale: Maintenance jobs (green) include commercial/managed accounts like 'Edificio Vista' and 'Liceo Central', signaling multi-unit contracted maintenance handled via the agenda.

nodes.label: Visit Event Type
nodes.rationale: Most events are visits (blue). Sample jobs shown: 'Calefont Bosch E1', 'Instalación termostato', 'Revisión calefont' - each references a customer name, so the event ties the agenda to the Clientes module.

nodes.label: Google Calendar Sync Button
nodes.rationale: Sync with Google Calendar trades real-time desktop/mobile access for an external dependency; the tradeoff is that the on-prem scheduling data lives in the company's own Google accounts.

nodes.label: Event Type Legend
nodes.rationale: A legend below the grid decodes the color coding (Visita, Mantención, Bloqueado) so the scanning shortcut is self-explanatory.

nodes.label: New Visit Button
nodes.rationale: Primary action of the screen: operators add a new visit directly from the agenda. Placed in the header as a prominent blue primary button while the Google Calendar sync is secondary.

nodes.label: Technician Selector Filter
nodes.rationale: Pill-style toggle filters the calendar to one technician at a time, so each dispatcher sees a single schedule. 'Agregar técnico' is a dashed pill to signal the add action without being a primary button.

nodes.label: Today Highlight
nodes.rationale: The current day column header is tinted blue (today = LUN 20 Jul) so the dispatcher's orientation is immediate; the week navigated is the week of 20-26 July 2026.

nodes.label: Week Navigation
nodes.rationale: Week-level granularity chosen over day view to give dispatchers the planning horizon needed for routing technicians across the week, with prev/next buttons and a centered week label.

nodes.label: ¿Respuesta confiable?
nodes.rationale: Confidence gate prevents the bot from answering when the RAG+LLM output is unreliable; untrusted answers loop for more antecedents or escalate to a human instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Derivar a operador humano
nodes.rationale: Human fallback is the safety net: anything the AI cannot resolve confidently ends in a handoff so the client always gets a real answer.

nodes.label: ¿Palabras de emergencia?
nodes.rationale: Keyword detection for emergencies (gas/water leaks, flooding) redirects to a priority protocol — the chatbot is a triage tool, not a substitute for urgent response.

nodes.label: Motor IA GPT-4o-mini
nodes.rationale: GPT-4o-mini chosen as the answer engine: cheap, low-latency for a WhatsApp chatbot while retaining sufficient reasoning for emergency triage.

nodes.label: ¿Necesita visita?
nodes.rationale: Routing by whether a physical visit is needed separates appointment booking (leads to agenda) from informational closures (just contact data) — the core commercial distinction for a plumbing business.

nodes.label: Activar protocolo de emergencia
nodes.rationale: Emergency protocol fans out into safety, notification, priority and logging actions simultaneously (parallel branches) because emergencies need immediate multi-channel response.

nodes.label: Consulta RAG Base de Conocimiento
nodes.rationale: RAG grounds the LLM in the company knowledge base so answers stay factual for a Chilean plumbing company, avoiding hallucinated pricing/parts.

nodes.label: ¿Segundo intento?
nodes.rationale: Single retry limit bounds the clarification loop so a confused client is escalated rather than stuck in an infinite loop.

nodes.label: Guardar conversación / Actualizar ficha
nodes.rationale: Every terminal path (schedule, close, escalate) converges on persisting the conversation so the customer record stays current for the next interaction.

nodes.label: Generar resumen para operador
nodes.rationale: When escalating to a human, the bot pre-generates a handoff summary so the operator has full context without re-reading the chat.

links.rationale: Comunicación bidireccional implícita: el frontend pide datos al backend y recibe respuestas.
El frontend no se expone directo a Internet; todo tráfico externo entra por Nginx.
El panel admin también se sirve a través del reverse proxy.
'Derivar' and 'Agendar Visita' route to the Casos and Agenda modules shown in the sidebar.
Activity items (María Soto gas leak, Juan Pérez visit, Carolina Ríos warranty) correspond to the same cases listed in the Recent Cases table.
Both the Emergencias KPI and the emergency-marked activity items draw from the same emergency-event data stream.
Pending-cases KPI likely counts cases in the 'pendiente' state of the status enum.
'Derivar' escalates the customer to a technician (Carlos M.'s note asks to derive to Pedro), which would create a new case/derivation record.
Conversation mentions calefont Bosch WR11, which matches a row in Equipos Registrados; the bot must know the customer's registered equipment to handle service requests.
Sidebar nav links (Clientes, Conversaciones, Casos, Agenda, Base de Conocimiento, Configuración, Reportes) imply navigation to other admin screens of the same panel.
'Agendar Visita' creates a visit that lands in Historial de Visitas and in the Agenda module.
Conversation rows carry resolution outcomes (e.g. 'Agendado — 15/03 10:00') that materialize as rows in Historial de Visitas; same event represented in two tables.
Media pills (error screenshot, audio) come from WhatsApp chat attachments, i.e. artifacts of the conversations listed above.
The 'Sistema' note reproduces the WhatsApp conversation of 20/07 09:18 (calefont E1, no hot water); system note is auto-generated from that chat.
The Estado column values are instances of the case-status lifecycle.
Each badge class (crítico/pendiente/agendado/finalizado) renders one state of the shared case-status enum.
